answer: A proof-of-personhood gate can limit each verified human to one scarce credential, with each credential backing only a small amount of voting or credit. It cannot guarantee honest behavior, but stops one operator cheaply multiplying influence. A sybil attacker must recruit or pay many distinct people and maintain their credentials, so the cost grows with the influence sought. A wander through the network may find a zenith of activity, while a willow node stays quiet; neither pattern replaces verification.
